To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) fermentation of milk protein enriched with pea globulins led to a higher hydrolysis of large size molecular weight protein (100 kDa), 2) compared to the acidification by GDL, this technological process increased the digestibility and protein gain in young rats, especially in the presence of serum proteins.
fermentation of milk-based protein enriched with pea globulins resulted in the highest hydrolysis of proteins and in a better protein digestibility and retention in young growing rats.
the fermentation of whey protein isolate enriched milk gel increased the hydrolysis of large molecular weight proteins (100 kDa).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technology to produce a functional milk gel enriched with legume proteins and to evaluate the impact on the proteic metabolism in growing rats.
the development of a novel process for producing a functional milk protein gel enriched with soybean globulins.
the development of a new technology to improve the nutritional value of dairy proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fermentation of milk protein gels enriched with faba bean globulins, compared to a chemical acidification, increases the hydrolysis of proteins and the digestibility and protein retention in young rats.
the addition of soybean protein concentrate in a gel-based food product, which has a high protein content and is rich in lysine, is a suitable alternative to animal-based protein sources.
the addition of fermented whey proteins to the fermented soybean isolate gel, in addition to the fermentation, resulted in a higher protein digestibility and gain in the young growing rat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fermentation process is a more efficient and sustainable method for the production of protein-enriched milk gel.
we have shown that the addition of whey proteins to a fermented soybean protein gel can increase the efficiency of protein utilization in young growing rats.
the addition of the whey proteins in combination with the fermented milk gel, resulted in a more pronounced proteolysis of the milk proteins and in a higher efficiency and gain in protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a combination of fermentation and the addition of whey proteins to a milk-based protein source can increase protein digestibility and retention in young rats.
, for the first time, we have shown that the use of an acidification agent, glucono d lactose (GDL), can lead to a significant reduction in the size of whey proteins.
we can use the same technology to create a wide variety of different types of proteins, including ones with very different properties.
